name: Tomatillos
tile_uses: Salsa verde, tacos, rice bowls, chicken
why_now: Tomatillos run from midsummer into October and are at their best right now — heavy, tight in the husk, and tart in a way that no other ingredient in the basket is. They are also the cheapest sauce you can make from scratch.
how_to_choose: The husk should be tight and papery, not shriveled or loose
The fruit should fill its husk completely
Firm, with a slight tackiness underneath — that is normal, rinse it off
Bright green, not yellowing; yellow means sweeter and duller
Small ones are usually tarter than large ones
buy_this_much: 1 lb. That is one batch of salsa verde, which is about a week's worth.
price_note: Inexpensive year-round and especially now. A pound of tomatillos makes more salsa than a jar of it costs.

flavor_paths.name: Boiled
flavor_paths.description: Simmered until olive-colored, then blended. Softer, rounder, the everyday version.

flavor_paths.name: Charred
flavor_paths.description: Blistered in a dry pan first. Smokier and darker. The July technique, again.

flavor_paths.name: Raw
flavor_paths.description: Blended straight, uncooked. Sharpest of the three. Good on rich meat, hard on eggs.

weekday_uses: Simmered with chicken thighs until the sauce thickens
weekend_use: Simmer a pot of chicken thighs in salsa verde for an hour and shred them. It is the easiest thing in this edition and it feeds you for days.
storage: Leave the husks on and keep them in a paper bag in the crisper — two weeks, easily. Husked, they go sticky and soft faster. Blended salsa keeps five days.
one_thing_to_learn: Tomatillos are not unripe tomatoes. They are a different plant, related to the ground cherry, and the sourness is structural rather than a sign that you got there too early. That means you cannot fix a tomatillo by waiting. What you can do is decide how much of that sharpness you want: raw keeps all of it, boiling rounds it off, charring trades some of it for smoke.
market_question: Were these picked this week? And do you cook yours or use them raw?
